Grave Matters Roadmap

Development roadmap · Prototype v0.5.1

Grave Matters, Inc.

A cemetery tycoon where the customers never really leave.

Sell plots to the living by day, keep the dead content by night. This page is the plan: what's built so far, what I'm testing right now, and the road to a full release on Steam.

  • NowPrototype v0.5.1, out with playtesters
  • NextLock the look, then build the first finished cemetery as a free demo
  • GoalVersion 1.0 on Steam, roughly two years away

What the game is about

Four ideas every feature has to serve. If something doesn't serve any of them, it doesn't go in.

Every grave tells a story

Residents have names, quirks, friends, feuds and unfinished business. You should remember who's buried where.

Two worlds, one cemetery

Who you bury where by day decides who argues and who performs at night, and trouble at night spills back into the day.

Clever, but always readable

The neighbor puzzle can get deep, but the game always shows exactly why a ghost feels the way it does.

Cozy, with a chill

Darkly funny, never gory. The jokes land on the ghosts, never on the mourners.

The road ahead

Six stages, in order. Each one ends when a clear test is met, not on a date.

  1. you are here
    1

    Find the fun

    Nowabout 2 to 3 months

    Small prototypes, played by real people, to learn what's fun before building anything big. Five versions so far, each shaped by playtest logs.

    Done when testers play for 45 minutes or more without being asked, can explain the day and night loop in their own words, and each experiment below has a clear winner.

  2. 2

    Lay the foundations

    Nextabout 3 to 4 months

    Settle the art and sound style, rebuild the code on solid ground (moddable content, more save slots, room for translations), and finish the first cemetery at full quality. That cemetery becomes the free demo, and the Steam page goes up.

    Done when someone watching the demo can't tell it's unfinished.

  3. 3

    Build it all

    about 8 to 11 months

    Every system and every campaign cemetery: building where you like, funerals, star ghosts with stories of their own, night attractions, staff with skills and moods, events, and a campaign with a mystery running through it.

    Done when the whole campaign plays from start to finish, even with some placeholder art.

  4. 4

    Make it shine

    about 5 to 7 months

    Final art, music and writing, balancing, accessibility options, translations and Steam Deck support, then a closed beta.

    Done when the beta players' biggest complaints are fixed.

  5. 5

    Open the gates

    alongside the polish

    The demo at a Steam Next Fest, a trailer, and then release.

  6. 6

    Keep the lamps lit

    after launch

    Fixes and free updates, an expansion, mod support, and more platforms.

All timings are rough estimates, not promises. Altogether, about two years to version 1.0.

So far

Each prototype added a layer, and each one went to playtesters before the next began.

  1. v0.1

    The first churchyard

    One cemetery, day and night, six ghost personalities, staff, night tours, wishes, ghosts moving on, and three stars to earn in a week.

  2. v0.2

    The middle of the week

    Friendships and feuds between neighbors, a breakdown of every ghost's mood, event cards with choices, the first story (Captain Brine's lost will), and saving.

  3. v0.3

    The last stretch

    A reputation that fades unless you keep earning it, wealthy families with two wishes, eleven event cards, an All Hallows' Eve finale, upgrades, and free play after the verdict. Then a round of fixes from the first playtests.

  4. v0.4

    Experiments

    A second cemetery, two new ghost personalities, an option to let families choose their own plots, and nights that grow restless toward the finale.

  5. v0.5

    Funerals and options

    Undertakers who lead every funeral, an office clerk who places the families you haven't got to, and a choice of day length and how strict the board is. Then a round of fixes from four playtests, including a warning before the council closes you down.

Being tested right now

Versions 0.4 and 0.5 try several big ideas at once. Playtests decide which ones stay.

A second cemetery: Saltmarsh Point

A windy clifftop churchyard with a lighthouse. Plots in single rows have only two neighbors, while the middle of a three-by-three square has four. Families who want a water view ask for the sea.

Does the neighbor puzzle hold up on a different shape?

Pranksters and Romantics

Pranksters play tricks on the neighbors at night: jolly ghosts laugh along, grumpy and shy ones fume. Two Romantics side by side become sweethearts, and they'd rather move on together. Send one on alone and the other is heartbroken.

Can players read these without a tutorial? How many personalities is too many?

Who picks the plot?

By default you place every family yourself. One option lets each family look around and buy the plot they like best, with no thought for the neighbors, while you rope off plots you'd rather keep. Or stay in charge and hire an office clerk, who places any family you haven't got to in time, wherever everyone will be happiest.

Which takes away the busywork without taking away control? Bigger cemeteries will need one of these.

Funerals with an undertaker

Hire an undertaker and every burial becomes a small funeral: the undertaker meets the family at the gate, wheels the coffin to the grave on a bier and reads a short service. The new ghost starts out happier and the town takes note. Each undertaker leads one funeral at a time, so busy days call for two.

Is the procession a pleasure to watch, or just a delay?

Your pace, your rules

A new week starts with a few choices. Short, normal or long days, with the goals scaled to match. And a strict board that closes you down if the money or the town's goodwill runs out, or a relaxed one that only gives its verdict at the end of the week.

Which settings do players pick, and do they keep playing longer?

Still to try before this stage ends

  • Laying out plots anywhere on your land instead of in fixed sections.
  • A second mood scale for energy, so a ghost can be happy and still too tired to perform.

What version 1.0 should hold

The plan for launch. More comes in updates afterwards, and playtesting can still change these numbers.

  • 5
    campaign cemeteries, each with its own goals
  • 10
    ghost personalities
  • 15
    star ghosts with stories to finish
  • 8
    buildings and night attractions
  • 40
    decorations
  • 12
    events with choices
  • 6
    staff roles
  • 8–12
    hours of campaign, plus a sandbox
  • Build where you like: plot types from single graves to family crypts, paths, fences and lighting
  • Ghosts who make friends, fall out, and fall in love, and remember it night after night
  • Night tours along routes you draw, with performers and attractions
  • Rules that place families for you as the cemetery grows
  • Map views for mood, beauty, lighting and staff, and a reason behind every number
  • Controller and Steam Deck support, achievements and cloud saves

After launch

  • UpdatesFixes from player feedback, then a free update with a new cemetery and theme.
  • An expansionA bigger themed addition, such as a pirates' resting place or a seasonal haunting.
  • Mods and more platformsCustom ghosts, decorations and scenarios, plus Mac and Linux, and consoles later on.

Want to help shape it?

The best thing right now is playtesting. Play a week in the current prototype on Windows and send the short log it writes, along with what you enjoyed, what confused you, and when (if ever) you got bored. Reply to the post that brought you here and I'll send you the download.

See you at the gate.
